drop_predicate.detected_within: the release must occur within the environment's own registered episode horizon; its confirmation window may extend up to drop_confirm_ticks past it
drop_predicate.owner: this project (the environment scores placement, not custody)
drop_predicate.plain_english: it was being held, it was off the table, it left the hand, it stayed out of the hand, and it was not at the goal
drop_predicate.reads: mujoco MjData.contact, the engine's own contact list; no vision, no heuristic, no policy introspection
drop_predicate.rule: a release is proposed at control tick k when the block was in contact with BOTH gripper finger pads at tick k-1, AND its centre was more than airborne_margin_m above its resting height on the table at tick k-1, AND at tick k MuJoCo reports it in contact with fewer than both pads, AND the environment's own info['is_success'] is false at tick k. It is CONFIRMED as a drop only if, over the following drop_confirm_ticks, the grasp is not regained and the block is at some tick in contact with nothing at all. Otherwise it is discarded.

severity_proxy.definition: the block's world-frame linear speed (its free joint's linear dof velocity, exact for a free body) at the last control tick at which it was still unsupported, i.e. immediately before its first contact with the table or the floor after the drop
severity_proxy.sampling_note: speed is sampled at the 40 ms control tick, so a free fall gains about 0.39 m/s between samples; the reported value is the last sample before contact, never an extrapolation
severity_proxy.secondary_definition: block centre height at the drop minus its centre height at that first contact

drop_predicate.why_confirmation: MuJoCo's contact list can drop one pad for a single tick while the block is still pinched and being carried upward; without the confirmation window that artefact would be sold as a drop

frames.note: control runs at 25 Hz, already a sensible replay rate, so no decimation is applied

published_conditions.note: None means the publisher states nothing about that axis
published_conditions.prose: unmodified Gymnasium-Robotics FetchPickAndPlace-v4: the shipped 2 kg block, shipped friction, the environment's own block and goal sampling, no action noise, no control latency

compat_shim.what: the module-global name `mujoco` inside gymnasium_robotics.utils.mujoco_utils is rebound to a proxy that forwards every attribute to the real mujoco module except `mjtJoint`, whose four members are plain Python ints
compat_shim.why: gymnasium-robotics 1.4.2 guards its joint-slot arithmetic with `assert joint_type in (mujoco.mjtJoint.mjJNT_HINGE, mujoco.mjtJoint.mjJNT_SLIDE)`; on mujoco 3.13.0 that containment test is False for the numpy int32 the model returns, even though the corresponding `==` is True. The environment cannot be constructed at all.

goal_marker.note: drawn at `goal_m`, which is fixed for the whole episode

mutations.note: mass and friction are written into the compiled model; the offset is written into the block's free joint after reset. Nothing else in the scene is touched.

success_predicate.block_position_source: obs['achieved_goal'], which is the environment's own read of the block's site. NOTE: after mujoco.mj_step the kinematics cache (xpos, site_xpos, contacts) is one 2 ms physics substep behind qpos, because mj_step evaluates forward dynamics and then integrates. The environment computes is_success from that cache, so this project does too — comparing the environment's boolean against a position recomputed from qpos instead disagrees on about one tick in a thousand, purely where the distance sits within ~2 mm of the 50 mm threshold. The skew is 1.4 mm at 0.7 m/s, far below every threshold used here (the airborne margin is 30 mm).
success_predicate.block_velocity_source: the block's free-joint linear dof velocity from qvel, exact for a free body; the environment publishes only a dt-scaled site velocity, so there is no environment-owned alternative
success_predicate.no_bespoke_detector: this project implements no placement detector; it records the environment's flag and cross-checks it at every tick against the distance recomputed from the environment's OWN achieved_goal and desired_goal

target.evaluated_by: numpy reimplementation of stable_baselines3.SACPolicy.predict; torch is not a run-time dependency
target.evaluation: deterministic mean action, tanh-squashed then unscaled to the action box
target.feature_extractor: CombinedExtractor (parameter-free: flatten + concat in sorted key order)

alternatives_considered.why_not_primary: trained on FetchPickAndPlace-v1 (the mujoco-py environment, no longer installable) and behind sb3_contrib's TimeFeatureWrapper, so running it needs both an environment-version transplant and a wrapper reimplementation, and its published mean_reward was measured on an environment that cannot be run here — it cannot serve as a check on this harness
trained on the right environment version, but publishes only best_model.zip with no config and no eval protocol, so there is less to pin and nothing to reproduce
published mean_reward -12.70 +/- 12.81; the spread implies failed episodes at nominal

termination_rules.settle_note: stepping continues past the horizon only after a drop, until the block has landed plus 5 ticks, capped at 30 ticks. The policy keeps acting throughout; nothing is frozen or scripted, and a drop is never detected in the settle window.
